newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends steady on low dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends steady on low dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed barely moved against the dollar on Wednesday, in range-bound trade due to a lack of demand for the greenback and stable money rates, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.43 to the dollar, after opening at 58.42, they said.
"The dollar-rupee exchange rate hardly moved because speculators were out and there was not enough import covering demand either," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
"Since all banks are long on dollars, there are ample sellers at around current levels to fill small import bills," he added.
Dealers expect the exchange rate to remain range-bound this week, in the absence of a big import bill or overseas movement by the dollar.
Overnight call money closed at 9.5 percent after opening at 10, with the market well offered.
The Central Bank's overnight repurchase rate was at nine percent.
